sections.Kurzabstract: The EFK is a short, cross-disease screening instrument and assesses the illness coping behaviour of visually impaired patients. With 45 items, the EFK assesses the following nine coping domains at the emotional, cognitive and behavioural level: (1) Acting, problem-oriented coping, (2) Distance and self-building, (3) Information seeking and exchange of experience, (4) Trivialization, wishful thinking and threat denial, (5) Depressive coping, (6) Willingness to accept help, (7) Active search for social integration, (8) Trust in medical skill, (9) Working out an inner hold. Reliability: Internal consistency for all patients lies between alpha = .65 (scale "Vertrauen in die ärztliche Kunst") and alpha = .80 (scales "Handelndes, problemorientiertes Coping" and "Vertrauen in die ärztliche Kunst"). Validity: A factor-analytic examination (varimax rotation) yielded a 12-factor structure. Correlations (Pearson) were computed with the Freiburger Fragebogen zur Krankheitsverarbeitung (FKV-LIS) and the Fragebogen zur sozialen Unterstützung (F-SOZU).
sections.Diagnostische Zielsetzung: The EFK is a cross-disease screening instrument in paper-pencil format that is suitable for individual testing. It serves to assess a person's current coping efforts at the emotional, cognitive and behavioural level.
sections.Aufbau: With 45 items, the EFK assesses nine coping domains: (1) Acting, problem-oriented coping, (2) Distance and self-building, (3) Information seeking and exchange of experience, (4) Trivialization, wishful thinking and threat denial, (5) Depressive coping, (6) Willingness to accept help, (7) Active search for social integration, (8) Trust in medical skill, (9) Working out an inner hold. The items are answered on a five-point rating scale (0 = not at all to 4 = very much).
sections.Grundlagen und Konstruktion: The test construction is based on classical test theory.
sections.Empirische Prüfung und Gütekriterien:
Reliability: Internal consistency for all patients lies between α = .65 (scale "Vertrauen in die ärztliche Kunst") and α = .80 (scales "Handelndes, problemorientiertes Coping" and "Vertrauen in die ärztliche Kunst").
Validity: A factor-analytic examination (varimax rotation) yielded a 12-factor structure. Correlations (Pearson) were computed with the FKV-LIS and the F-SOZU-LIS. Evidence of convergent and divergent as well as factorial and differential validity could be found.
Norms: Stanine scores are available for the total sample of 1 815.
sections.Testkonzept/Theoretischer Hintergrund:
With the Essener Fragebogen zur Krankheitsverarbeitung (EFK), Franke and Jagla established in 2016 a cross-disease questionnaire that serves to assess a person's current coping efforts for dealing with illness at the emotional, cognitive and behavioural level.
Illness coping as such is defined according to Mayer and Filipp (2002, S. 307) as "... all those attempts [...] that people employ in the context of an illness to deal with the internal and external demands that arise in this life situation". In this context, the increase in chronic diseases in particular must be mentioned (Bengel et al., 2003). Chronic illnesses subsequently go along with manifold physical and psychosocial limitations. Accordingly, adequate assessment of psychological aspects such as illness coping can go along with increased adherence, adjustment and an improvement in quality of life (Härter, 2000, 2002).
For the construction and item generation of the EFK, the following instruments, which likewise address the assessment of illness coping, were critically analysed:
(1) Skala zur Erfassung des Bewältigungsverhaltens (SEBV; Ferring & Filipp, 1989)
(2) Fragebogen zur Erfassung der Formen von Krankheitsbewältigung (FEKB; Klauer, Filipp & Ferring, 1989)
(3) Trierer Skalen zur Krankheitsbewältigung (TSK; Klauer & Filipp, 1993)
(4) Short form of the Freiburger Fragebogen zur Krankheitsverarbeitung (FKV-LIS; Muthny, 1989).
In particular for the FKV and TSK, sufficient statistics for reliability and validity could not be demonstrated in several studies (Hardt, et al., 2003).
sections.Testkonzept/Testaufbau:
The EFK was developed as a short screening instrument with 45 items. In the form of a questionnaire, the test comprises nine a priori constructed scales with five items each on the following areas (Franke & Jagla, 2016, S. 6-7):
(1) Acting, problem-oriented coping (HPC): active, cognitively structuring coping work
(2) Distance and self-building (AUS): search for self-affirmation and encouragement as well as distraction, distance and self-building strategies
(3) Information seeking and exchange of experience (IUE): active search for information about one's own illness in conversation with other affected persons and the search for literature
(4) Trivialization, wishful thinking and threat denial (BWB): blocking out and ignoring as well as daydreams and playing down
(5) Depressive coping (DV): self-pity and withdrawal are asked about
(6) Willingness to accept help (BAH): the inner willingness to open up to others and to accept their support, or creation of new social contacts
(8) Trust in medical skill (VIÄ): trust in the work of the physicians as well as compliance
(9) Working out an inner hold (EIH): working out an inner hold through religious or alternative ego-strengthening behaviour patterns.
These areas have proven sufficiently stable in terms of test theory (Franke & Jagla, 2016).
sections.Testkonzept/Auswertungsmodus:
For scoring the EFK, sum scores are computed across all items of a scale. The sum scores are then divided by the number of items, five, of each of the nine scales (Franke & Jagla, 2016).

sections.Testkonzept/Auswertungshilfen: Scoring aids are available in the form of tables of standard values in the test manual and as a separate file under "Downloads". The manual indicates the reversal of two items from the area VIÄ (Franke & Jagla, 2016).
sections.Testkonzept/Auswertungszeit: Completion of the EFK requires approx. 10 minutes.
sections.Durchführung/Testformen: The EFK is available as a screening instrument for individual testing.
sections.Durchführung/Altersbereiche: The EKF has so far been used with adolescents aged 16 and older and with young adults.
sections.Durchführung/Durchführungszeit: Answering the questionnaire takes less than ten minutes.
sections.Durchführung/Material: Completion takes place in paper-pencil format. A scoring aid is available for the screening instrument.
sections.Durchführung/Instruktion:
Patients are to tick the answer that applies best to them on the 5-point Likert scale (scaling: 0 = „überhaupt nicht“ to 4 = „sehr stark“) and are asked to answer every question. They are informed that the questionnaire sheds light on their current way of dealing with their own illness.
An example instruction reads: „Wie gehen Sie zurzeit mit Ihrer Erkrankung um? Bitte lesen Sie jede Aussage durch, und entscheiden Sie durch ein Kreuz, inwieweit sie auf Sie zutrifft.“
sections.Durchführung/Durchführungsvoraussetzunge: No special administration requirements are stated.
sections.Testkonstruktion: The test construction of the EFK is based on classical test theory. The EFK is based on central analysis samples for development that were collected between 1995 and 2015 with a total of N = 1 815 inpatients and outpatients. At the Eye Clinic of the University Hospital Essen, data on n = 555 patients with chronic eye disease aged between 16 and 86 years (42.9 % men, 57.1 % women) were collected for the first data set in the period 1995 to 2005. In addition, n = 529 patients with chronic renal insufficiency before or after transplantation were included in the survey (56.3 % men, 43.7 % women). A mixed subsample was acquired in the period 2000 to 2015 from n = 731 chronically ill persons from inpatient and outpatient healthcare facilities, predominantly in Saxony-Anhalt (48 % men, 52 % women). The clinical pictures of this sample come from the areas of internal medicine, gynaecology, neurology and orthopaedics (Jagla & Franke, 2009, 2012; Franke & Jagla, 2016).
sections.Gütekriterien/Objektivität: Administration, scoring and interpretation objectivity are sufficiently given.
sections.Gütekriterien/Reliabilität:
(1) Psychometric statistics based on the total sample.
First, reliability values of the individual scales are presented with regard to the total sample:
HPC: Acting, problem-oriented coping (Cronbach's α = .80)
AUS: Distance and self-building (α = .64)
IUE: Information seeking and exchange of experience (α = .79)
BWB: Trivialization, wishful thinking and threat denial (α = .51)
DV: Depressive coping (α = .74)
BAH: Willingness to accept help (α = .65)
ASS: Active search for social support (α = .78)
VIÄ: Trust in medical skill (α = .65)
EIH: Working out an inner hold (α = .65).
In summary, the reliability statistics are above .70 for four scales - HPC, IUE, DV and ASS - and above .60 for four scales - AUS, BAH, VIÄ and EIH. The scale BWB shows an internal consistency of only .51 (Franke & Jagla, 2016).
The 45 items were subjected to an exploratory factor analysis with subsequent varimax rotation in the total sample. This yielded ten factors with an eigenvalue λ ≥ 1 (eigenvalues 8.8, 3.8, 2.3, 2.1, 1.9, 1.6, 1.4, 1.3, 1.2, 1.0) (Franke & Jagla, 2016). In addition, five dimensions could be extracted by means of the scree test, which together could explain 45.7 % of the variance. In the course of the factor analysis, the EFK was reduced to five factors. After the analysis, factor 1 "Soziale Unterstützung" was assigned eleven items, factor 2 "Vertrauen und Tatkraft" ten, factor 3 "Informations- und Sinnsuche" eight, factor 4 "Depressiv-bagatellisierende Verarbeitung" likewise eight and factor 5 "Misstrauen und Rückzug" four items.
It was concluded that, in addition to depressive (factor 4) and active (factor 2) strategies, further illness coping strategies were found, focusing in particular on active social life (factor 1) and the search for information and meaning (factor 3). Of relevance here is that in the results of the factor analysis the scales HPC, IUE, DV and ASS of the original version were found completely. Scale BAH showed four and the scales BWB and VIÄ showed three item loadings on one factor; item number 31 achieved a double loading on factors three and five. Three items did not reach the loading threshold of at least .40 (Franke & Jagla, 2016).
(2) Psychometric statistics based on the first examination.
The lack of studies on the illness coping of visually impaired patients prompted the authors to carry out a first central psychometric examination in this patient group (Franke, Mähner, Reimer & Spangemacher, 2000). The EFK was examined with regard to its reliability and validity in a sample of N = 210 visually impaired persons. This consists of 117 patients with malignant choroidal melanoma following radioapplicator therapy (48.7 % men, 51.3 % women, mean age early 60s) as well as 93 patients with degenerative retinal diseases of various origins in middle age (64.5 % men, 35.5 % women, mean age late 40s). Both patient groups accordingly suffered from an impairment of vision that had developed in adulthood and affects (at least) one diseased eye. With the exception of one female patient, the questionnaire could be read and completed by all themselves.
As a result, a factor-analytic examination with subsequent varimax rotation carried out here also yielded 12 factors with an eigenvalue λ ≥ 1 (eigenvalues 10.8, 3.8, 2.6, 2.2, 1.8, 1.7, 1.6, 1.3, 1.2, 1.2, 1.1, 1.0). These could explain 66 % of the variance. In the scree test, seven factors were extracted here, on which the scales HPC, IUE, DV and VIÄ loaded on one factor and showed good reliability values.
For the scales AUS, BWB, ASS and EIH, four of the five items each and for the scale BAH three of five items grouped on one factor with good to satisfactory reliability.
sections.Gütekriterien/Validität:
Finally, results from the subsamples are to be used with regard to the examination of construct validity. In the study of N = 210 patients with eye disease, correlations (Pearson) were computed with the Freiburger Fragebogen zur Krankheitsverarbeitung (Liste) (FKV-LIS; Muthny, 1989) and the Fragebogen zur sozialen Unterstützung (F-SOZU-LIS; Fydrich, Sommer & Brähler, 2007). Hypothetically expected correlations between EFK scales with content closely corresponding to scales of the FKV-LIS could be confirmed. In addition, positive correlations of the scales ASS and DV with the F-SOZU-LIS could be demonstrated. These results support the view of Weber (1990) that an illness can be coped with through integration into social contexts (Franke, Mähner, Reimer, Spangemacher, & Esser, 2000).
In the subsample of N = 529 patients with chronic renal insufficiency, the correlations between the EFK and the scales of the Brief Symptom Checkliste (BSCL; Franke, 2016, formerly BSI; Franke, 1997) as well as the total score of social support F-SOZU with 22 items (Fydrich et al., 2007) were computed.

A group of 48 patients was surveyed with the EFK at the beginning and at the end of neurological rehabilitation phase II (Müller, Jagla, Riedel & Franke, 2014). The patients had the cerebrovascular conditions stroke and cerebral haemorrhage, the diseases of the nervous system multiple sclerosis, polyneuropathy and epilepsy, or the intracranial injury traumatic brain injury. The means on the scales ASS, AUS, HPC and BAH rose statistically significantly by the end of the rehabilitation measure. According to reports of the neurological patients, by the end of the complex intervention they more actively sought social support, engaged in more distraction and self-building, used active, problem-oriented coping strategies more strongly and were more willing to accept help and to seek information about the illness (Franke & Jagla, 2016). Thus, the stanine scores of these scales rose on average from stanine = 4 to stanine = 5 and moved more clearly towards the average range of values. The scores decreased most on the scale trust in medical skill, from rounded stanine = 5 to rounded stanine = 3 and thus to an approximately below-average value. These change measurements are of particular importance from the perspective of medical or rehabilitation psychology (Franke & Jagla, 2016).
In conclusion, the EFK shows sufficient sensitivity to change (Franke & Jagla, 2016).
sections.Anwendungsmöglichkeiten:
The Essener Fragebogen zur Krankheitsverarbeitung can be used with patients with all chronic physical illnesses and is a sensitive indicator in this area. The instrument has already proven itself in this respect in application.
With regard to use in acutely physically ill and mentally ill persons, no scientific publications are available so far.
The EFK is easy to use and has high acceptance among patients. Versions in German, English and Turkish are available (Franke & Jagla, 2016).
Previous fields of application of the EFK are:
Transplantation medicine (focus in the clinical area):
1.1. routine use, alongside the BSCL (Franke, 2016) and other instruments, in the Innsbruck programme to examine potential reconstructive transplantation patients psychologically-diagnostically (Hautz et al., 2010, 2011; Jagla, Reimer, Philipp & Franke, 2009; Kumnig et al., 2012)
1.2. examination of patients who were on the waiting list for a donor kidney or liver (Wick, Bauer, Malessa, Settmacher, & Strauß, 2015)
1.3. studies on the use of the EFK in kidney transplantation in Austria (Kumnig et al., 2012) and Germany (Bernhardt et al., 2010; Franke, 2010), in particular for assessing quality of life during dialysis (Franke, 2010)
1.4. use for assessing the psychosocial reactions of living kidney donors and living kidney donation recipients (Kumnig et al., 2014)
1.5. also use in reconstructive hand transplantation (Kumnig et al., 2012)
Gynaecology:
2.1. patients of inpatient gynaecology (Jagla et al., 2012, 2013)
2.2. patients with polycystic ovary syndrome (Jauca, Jäger, & Franke, 2010)
Oncology with HIV:
3.1. oncological patients (Berend, 2005)
3.2. persons affected by HIV (Jagla, Aldridge, & Merz, 2014; Ronel, 2003)
Neurology & ophthalmology:
4.1. neurological patients (Müller et al., 2014)
4.2. use for the first examination of the Essener Fragebogen zur Krankheitsverarbeitung (EFK) in visually impaired patients (Franke, Mähner, Reimer, Spangemacher & Esser, 2000)
4.3. The use in ophthalmology with patients in general (Franke, Mähner, Reimer, Voigtländer-Fleiß & Esser, 2003) and specifically with those affected by uveitis is discussed (Franke, Schütte & Heiligenhaus, 2005; Khanfer, Wallace, Keane & Philips, 2012; Schütte, Heiligenhaus & Franke, 2004)
4.4. use as a psychodiagnostic approach to assessing losses in health-related quality of life with reduced vision (Franke, Mähner, Reimer, Voigtländer-Fleiß & Esser, 2003)
4.5. use in Parkinson's disease (Liebermann, Witte & Prell, 2020)
Various groups:
5.1. various groups of patients (Jagla et al., 2009)
5.2. use as a psychological-diagnostic instrument for assessing stress and illness coping in the German-speaking area, associations between coping with a parent's mental illness and the health-related quality of life of the children (Jeske, Bullinger, Plaß, Petermann & Wiegand-Grefe, 2009)
5.3. use in complementary and alternative medicine in patients with primary immunodeficiency (Harasim et al., 2021)
5.4. use for assessing illness perception and coping in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (Vaske, Kenn, Keil, Rief, & Stenzel, 2016, 2017)
5.5. use in rheumatism patients (Vollmann, Pukrop, & Salewski, 2016) or pain patients (Franke, Nentzl, Küch & Jagla, 2020).
sections.Bewertung: The psychometric analyses mentioned overall support the use of the EFK to assess illness coping mechanisms in somatically ill patients. However, studies with further, not yet examined clinical pictures are necessary in order to be able to judge the usefulness of the EFK for assessing illness coping even more precisely in future (Franke & Jagla, 2016).

Study.Description: The EFK is a short, cross-disease screening instrument and assesses the illness coping behaviour of visually impaired patients. With 45 items, the EFK assesses the following nine coping domains at the emotional, cognitive and behavioural level: (1) Acting, problem-oriented coping, (2) Distance and self-building, (3) Information seeking and exchange of experience, (4) Trivialization, wishful thinking and threat denial, (5) Depressive coping, (6) Willingness to accept help, (7) Active search for social integration, (8) Trust in medical skill, (9) Working out an inner hold. Reliability: Internal consistency for all patients lies between alpha = .65 (scale "Vertrauen in die ärztliche Kunst") and alpha = .80 (scales "Handelndes, problemorientiertes Coping" and "Vertrauen in die ärztliche Kunst"). Validity: A factor-analytic examination (varimax rotation) yielded a 12-factor structure. Correlations (Pearson) were computed with the Freiburger Fragebogen zur Krankheitsverarbeitung (FKV-LIS) and the Fragebogen zur sozialen Unterstützung (F-SOZU).

In conclusion, the EFK shows sufficient sensitivity to change (Franke & Jagla, 2016).
Study.AgeRange: Adolescents aged 16 and older and young adults
Study.Instructions: Wie gehen Sie zur Zeit mit Ihrer Erkrankung um? Bitte lesen Sie jede Aussage durch, und entscheiden Sie durch ein Kreuz, inwieweit sie auf Sie zutrifft

EFK01.Description: Ich suche in Büchern und Zeitschriften nach Informationen über meine Erkrankung

EFK02.Description: Ich besuche andere Menschen oder lade sie zu mir ein

EFK03.Description: Ich versuche, Abstand und Ruhe zu gewinnen

EFK04.Description: Ich mache Pläne und halte mich daran

EFK06.Description: Ich löse Schritt für Schritt die Probleme, die auf mich zukommen

EFK07.Description: Ich versuche, mich abzulenken und zu erholen

EFK08.Description: Ich tausche mit anderen Patienten Erfahrungen im Umgang mit der Krankheit aus

EFK09.Description: Ich besinne mich auf meine früheren Erfahrungen mit Schicksalsschlägen

EFK10.Description: Ich informiere mich über alternative Heil- und Behandlungsmethoden

EFK11.Description: Ich sammele mich innerlich durch Gebete, Meditation oder durch einen intensiven Kontakt zur Natur

EFK12.Description: Ich versuche, meine Probleme aktiv anzugehen

EFK13.Description: Ich will nicht wahrhaben, wie es um mich steht

EFK14.Description: Ich informiere mich über meine Krankheit und alles, was dazu gehört

EFK15.Description: Ich beginne, mich innerlich anderen Menschen gegenüber zu öffnen

EFK16.Description: Ich befolge sehr genau den ärztlichen Rat

EFK17.Description: Ich verlebe mit anderen Menschen sehr schöne Stunden

EFK18.Description: Ich beginne, mich selbst auch einmal zu verwöhnen

EFK19.Description: Ich bin im Grunde skeptisch, ob ich wirklich gut medizinisch behandelt werde

EFK20.Description: Ich suche Kontakt zu anderen Menschen, die Ähnliches erlebt haben

EFK21.Description: Ich reagiere gereizt und ungeduldig auf andere Menschen

EFK23.Description: Ich lebe einfach weiter, als wäre nichts geschehen

EFK25.Description: Ich beginne, mich selbst zu bemitleiden

EFK26.Description: Ich beginne, meine Situation realistisch zu beurteilen und danach zu handeln

EFK27.Description: Ich versuche herauszufinden, wie ich mich gut mit meiner Krankheit arrangieren kann

EFK28.Description: Ich beginne, in der Krankheit einen Sinn zu sehen

EFK29.Description: Ich ziehe mich von anderen Menschen zurück

EFK30.Description: Ich beginne, meine Gefühle anderen Menschen zu zeigen

EFK31.Description: Ich bete und suche Trost im Glauben

EFK33.Description: Ich mißtraue den Ärzten und lasse die Diagnose überprüfen

EFK34.Description: Ich nehme die Hilfe anderer Menschen an

EFK35.Description: Ich bin ärgerlich oder zornig auf mein Schicksal

EFK37.Description: Ich beginne, die Krankheit als Schicksal anzunehmen

EFK38.Description: Ich mache aktiv neue Bekanntschaften oder frische alte Bekanntschaften wieder auf

EFK39.Description: Ich spiele die Bedeutung und Tragweite herunter

EFK40.Description: Ich beginne nachzudenken und zu grübeln

EFK41.Description: Ich habe ein hohes Ausmaß an Vertrauen in meine medizinische Behandlung

EFK42.Description: Ich finde meine innere Stärke wieder

EFK43.Description: Ich denke einfach nicht mehr an meine Krankheit

EFK44.Description: Ich versuche, anderen Menschen zu helfen
